canonical_statement: The study benchmarks the serving cost of three agentic memory systems against rolling-window and full-history reference strategies, while pairing cost with answer accuracy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We benchmark the serving cost of agentic memory systems...pair each cost measurement with answer accuracy on the LoCoMo benchmark.

canonical_statement: The benchmark evaluates Mem0, Hindsight, and Mastra Observational Memory alongside a 10-turn rolling window and full-history resubmission.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We benchmark three memory systems: Mem0, Hindsight, and Mastra Observational Memory...two reference strategies.

canonical_statement: All evaluated systems use the same two answer-stage backbones, gpt-oss-20b and Gemma 4 26B A4B, each at low and medium reasoning effort; embeddings use pplx-embed-v1-0.6b.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All systems are evaluated under the same two backbones, gpt-oss-20b and Gemma 4 26B A4B, each at two reasoning-effort settings (low, medium).

canonical_statement: The core memory-system cost grid contains five cells: (N,L)=(15,50), (15,200), (100,100), (400,50), and (400,200), with 8 runs per cell.
Mastra Observational Memory adds (800,200) and (800,400) cost cells at 3 runs each to reach its threshold regime.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Mastra OM adds two cells, (800, 200) and (800, 400), at 3 reps to reach its threshold regime.

canonical_statement: The deterministic rolling-window and full-history baselines use eight cost cells at 2 runs each, including three matched-content cells beyond the core five.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The two deterministic baselines use eight cells at 2 reps: the five above plus three matched-content cells, (40, 250), (200, 50), (400, 25).

canonical_statement: Cost-benchmark dialogues are synthetically generated as two-speaker conversations, then cached so repeats and systems receive identical dialogue content for each (N,L,seed).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: each finished dialogue is cached so it is identical across repeats and across systems.

canonical_statement: Per-turn serving cost C is defined as total billable LLM input tokens across ingest, retrieval, and answer stages.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: let C be the total LLM input tokens billed across ingest, retrieval, and answer.

canonical_statement: The separable cost model is log(C+1)=a+p log(L+1)+q log(t+1), with separate message-size and conversation-depth terms.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: log(C+1) = a + p log(L+1) + q log(t+1)

canonical_statement: Held-out model validation uses leave-one-(N,L)-cell-out cross-validation and reports mean absolute percentage error on held-out cell mean per-turn cost.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we drop one (N,L) cell, refit Equation (1) on the rest, and predict the dropped cell’s mean per-turn cost.

canonical_statement: Confidence intervals for cost-model exponents use a cluster bootstrap with B=1,000 resamples of whole end-to-end runs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Confidence intervals for p and q come from a cluster bootstrap with B=1,000 resamples...resamples whole runs.

canonical_statement: Accuracy evaluation uses a stratified LoCoMo subset consisting of four full dialogues and 665 evaluated QA pairs, excluding Category-5 adversarial questions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: four full dialogues, 665 evaluated QA pairs

population.label: Stratified LoCoMo subset of four full dialogues

canonical_statement: The answer judge is gpt-oss-120b at temperature 0 with one judging pass per question, held fixed across setting cells.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The judge is gpt-oss-120b at temperature=0 with a single pass per question. We hold it fixed across all setting cells.

canonical_statement: Accuracy is the fraction of LoCoMo questions judged correct for a given system-setting cell.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Accuracy is the fraction of questions judged correct, reported per (system, setting) cell.

outcome.definition: Fraction of evaluated questions judged correct

canonical_statement: The joint cost-accuracy analysis pairs each system-setting cell with mean billable cost at the (N=100,L=100) reference cell and LoCoMo accuracy, and reports cost per correct answer as a derived statistic.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We report this joint matrix (Table 3) and the cost-per-correct-answer ratio C/Acc as the primary derived statistic.

canonical_statement: The cost benchmark uses synthetic rather than real conversations; content-dependent fact density or consolidation behavior may differ in real interactions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Memory fact extraction and memory consolidation rates depend on how many extractable facts appear per turn, and this density may differ in real conversations.

canonical_statement: Accuracy is reported only on the LoCoMo subset, so joint cost-accuracy claims do not directly transfer to task-oriented or knowledge-intensive QA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The joint claims hold for the LoCoMo distribution...and do not directly transfer to task-oriented or knowledge-intensive QA.

canonical_statement: The separable cost model is descriptive rather than mechanistic and has 0.18–0.69 leave-one-cell-out error for the three memory systems, so predictions at untested workloads are rough estimates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cost predictions for these three systems at untested (N,L) values should be read as rough estimates only.

canonical_statement: Hindsight’s ingest-stage backbone was not benchmark-controlled; its per-cell totals are reported, but cross-backbone and reasoning-effort comparisons for Hindsight are not valid within this benchmark.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Hindsight’s ingest backbone was not benchmark-controlled...exclude it from cross-backbone and reasoning-effort comparisons.

canonical_statement: Provider-routing fallback can change per-token rates and break prompt-cache reuse, introducing serving-cost variance not captured by a single contract-rate calculation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the primary provider can saturate and route requests to a fallback provider...A prefix cached at the primary provider does not hit on the fallback provider.

canonical_statement: Cost per correct answer is a partial quality metric because it ignores latency, retrieval payload size, answer-token budget, retrieval recall, and abstention behavior.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: It treats accuracy as the only quality measure and ignores latency, retrieval-payload size, answer-token budget, retrieval recall, and abstention behavior.

canonical_statement: For gpt-oss-20b full-history at (N=400,L=200), the serving stack rejected requests beyond turn 374 despite the authors estimating the true prompt at about 74,800 tokens; the paper treats this as a serving-stack error and makes no context-length claim.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We treat this as a serving-stack error, report gpt-oss-20b full-history costs only to turn 374, and make no context-length claim.

canonical_statement: Wilson confidence intervals in the accuracy table treat the 665 questions as independent and therefore understate uncertainty because questions are clustered within dialogues.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: they treat the 665 questions as independent and so understate uncertainty given dialogue-level clustering

canonical_statement: Conversation length and message size alone predict the two window-based reference strategies well but do not adequately predict memory-system serving cost, which the authors attribute to internal memory state.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The retrieval- and threshold-driven memory systems have 18–69% held-out error. This shows that their cost is driven by internal memory state, not by conversation length or message size.

canonical_statement: No single memory system is best across all settings; backbone choice and memory-system choice jointly determine the cost surface.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No single system is best in all settings...backbone and memory are a joint decision.

canonical_statement: A memory system becomes cheaper than full-history serving only after a workload-dependent break-even threshold that can be immediate for cheap systems or beyond 400 turns for expensive ones.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This threshold is immediate for the cheapest systems and beyond 400 turns for the most expensive.

canonical_statement: The authors disclose use of Claude Code (Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 4.6) for framing support, benchmark/analysis code, and manuscript drafting/revision, while stating that they reviewed and verified generated content.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the authors used Claude Code (Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 4.6) as an assistive tool.
